title: 2000 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: Consider these two geoboard quadrilaterals. Which of the following statements is true?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
The area of quadrilateral \(I\) is more than the area of
quadrilateral \(II.\)

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
The area of quadrilateral \(I\) is less than the area of
quadrilateral \(II.\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
The quadrilaterals have the same area and the same
perimeter.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
The quadrilaterals have the same area, but the perimeter of
\(I\) is more than the perimeter of \(II.\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
The quadrilaterals have the same area, but the
perimeter of \(I\) is less than the perimeter of \(II.\)

solutions.text:
Assume that the pegs on this grid are separated by \(1\) unit.

Note that region \(I\) is a parallelogram with base \(1\) and height \(1,\) making its area \(1 \cdot 1 = 1.\)

We can split region \(II\) into \(2\) triangles, both with base \(1\) and height \(1.\) This makes the sum of the areas \[ 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1. \] This shows that both regions have the same area.

Note that each region has \(2\) sides that are of length \(\sqrt{2}.\) Region \(I\) has \(2\) unit sides, whereas region \(II\) only has \(1.\)

The other side of region \(II\) is clearly greater than \(1,\) which shows that region \(II\) has the greater perimeter.

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Decompose both quadrilaterals into unit right triangles
Compute all four side lengths of each quadrilateral
